- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), particularly if recent prices are trending down; add 3–5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; if sentiment shifts sharply from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope to prevent overshoot.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending sideways, favor mean reversion by slightly lowering forecast toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast peak at +10% above recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.33 or below) over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 5–8% to reflect risk aversion.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly turning (e.g., 3 consecutive days >0.67 followed by 3 consecutive days <0.33); use smoother transition curves.
